item.title: Prabowo Guarantees Increased Regional Transfer Funds for Next Year
item.description: President Prabowo guarantees central government transfer funds to regions will not be cut and will increase next year, speaking at Rakornas TPAKD on Thursday.
item.content:encoded:
Guarantee for Regional Heads

President Prabowo Subianto assured regional leaders that funding flows from the central government to the regions will not be reduced. The guarantee was delivered directly before governors, regents, and mayors attending the 2026 National Coordination Meeting (Rakornas) of the Regional Financial Access Acceleration Team (TPAKD) at JIExpo Kemayoran, Central Jakarta, on Thursday (10/22/2026).

Prabowo asked regional leaders not to worry because money flowing to regencies would not be cut, pledging to prove it. He even promised that fund disbursements to regions would be larger next year. 'And in the coming year, I believe we will disburse even more,' he added.

Goal: Driving the Economy and Prosperity

Prabowo explained that increasing budget allocations to regions aims to drive the wheels of the economy while improving public welfare, directing all potential toward achieving a prosperous society. He stressed that public welfare is his primary objective as president.

The most poignant remarks came when he tied his presidency to the condition of the people. 'I want to be president to see my people prosper. If being president means my people remain poor, I do not want to be president. I would be ashamed. Better that I not be president,' he said, met with applause from regional heads.

Pride of Regional Leaders

Closing his address, Prabowo advised that the true pride of a regional leader comes when people smile during visits. He considered the public's smiles when leaders directly visit the field to be proof of a successful mandate.

The 2026 Rakornas TPAKD itself served as a central-regional coordination forum to accelerate regional financial access, which this year positioned poverty alleviation and local economic strengthening as top priorities. This guarantee of increased transfer funds is expected to provide fiscal certainty for regional governments in designing development programs and public services next year, particularly for regions that have relied on central transfers as the backbone of their Regional Revenues and Expenditures Budgets (APBD).

item.title: Juventus Held 2-2 by Rennes in Europa League
item.description: Juventus drew 2-2 with Stade Rennais on Europa League matchday 3 at Allianz Stadium, Thursday (23/10/2026) early morning WIB. Zeki Çelik (5') and Nick Woltemade's penalty (67') were cancelled out by Mousa Al Tamari (15') and Boulaye Dia's penalty (43'). Juventus have seven points from three league-phase games.
item.content:encoded:
Drama-Filled First Half

Juventus failed to win at home. Hosting Stade Rennais on matchday 3 of the 2026/2027 UEFA Europa League league phase at Allianz Stadium, Thursday (23/10/2026) early morning WIB, the Bianconeri had to settle for a 2-2 draw with the visitors from France.

Juventus struck early through Zeki Çelik in the 5th minute. But Rennes turned the game around before half-time: Mousa Al Tamari levelled in the 15th minute from Bryan Reynolds' pass, before Boulaye Dia converted a penalty in the 43rd minute to put the visitors 2-1 up. Çelik's early strike briefly had Allianz Stadium roaring, but Rennes' two replies silenced the home crowd.

Woltemade's Penalty Rescues a Point

Juventus hit back after the break. The hosts' pressure paid off in the 67th minute when Nick Woltemade calmly converted a penalty to make it 2-2. The score held until the final whistle despite Juventus pushing for a winner, including a VAR check in the 89th minute. Woltemade, on loan at Juventus from Newcastle United since the summer, rescued his side once again.

Federico Gatti's 19th-minute booking, goalkeeper Brice Samba's 20th-minute injury — he returned a minute later — and Al Tamari's 32nd-minute injury all marked the game. Rennes stayed disciplined in a 5-3-2 shape and nearly stole the win on the counter.

Seven Points from Three Games

The draw takes Juventus to seven points from three league-phase games, after a 5-0 win over NEC Nijmegen and a 2-1 victory at Celta Vigo. Rennes have five points from a goalless draw with Sturm Graz, a 2-1 win over OFI Crete, and the draw in Turin.

Failing to win at home is a concern for Juventus, who also lost 0-3 to Lazio in Serie A last weekend. Statistically, Juventus edged possession 51%-49% and both sides earned five corners, while Rennes actually managed more shots on target (5 to 4). A packed schedule awaits, with no less demanding away fixtures in both domestic and European competition.

item.title: US Bans BYD Electric Vehicles From Kadena Air Base
item.description: The US military will ban BYD electric vehicles from Kadena Air Base in Japan starting Oct 26, 2026, citing security concerns over sensitive data collection.
item.content:encoded:
Starting Monday, BYD Vehicles Turned Away at Kadena Gates

The United States' Kadena Air Base in Okinawa, Japan, will turn away all BYD electric vehicles starting Monday (10/26/2026). This zero-exception ban was reported by South Korea's Yonhap news agency on Friday (10/23/2026), citing a US military official stationed in Japan.

The policy covers vehicles belonging to base personnel, contractors, commercial entities, and even taxis. The US military in Japan has not provided official confirmation of this report, and BYD has not responded to requests for comment.

Cameras and Sensors Prompt Security Concerns

According to Yonhap, security concerns center on the cameras and sensors installed on BYD vehicles. US officials assess that these devices could potentially collect and leak sensitive security information from inside the base.

The ban follows an action by the US Department of Defense in June 2026 adding BYD—alongside Alibaba, Baidu, and NIO—to a list of companies allegedly aiding the Chinese military. BYD denied the allegations, calling them groundless. Alibaba has even sued the US government, while China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs protested the list as discriminatory and unreasonable.

A similar situation has emerged in South Korea: around 190 Chinese-made connected vehicles, including BYD models, have reportedly entered South Korean military facilities—ranging from the Ministry of National Defense to an F-35 fighter jet base. South Korea's Defense Ministry is now preparing restrictions through amendments to defense security directives. The United Kingdom had also previously restricted Chinese-technology vehicles within its ministerial fleet.

item.title: Kanye West: 360-Degree Dome Stage Ready at GBK, Concert on October 24
item.description: Raw Vision Collective promoter has confirmed that Kanye West's viral 360-degree dome stage (globe) is ready at GBK Main Stadium for the YE Live in Jakarta concert on Saturday, October 24, 2026 — Ye's debut performance in Indonesia and the only Southeast Asian city on his official tour.
item.content:encoded:
Dome Stage Ready Two Days Before Concert

JAKARTA — Promoter Raw Vision Collective has confirmed that the viral 360-degree dome stage (globe) belonging to Kanye West is ready to be installed at Gelora Bung Karno (GBK) Main Stadium, Senayan, Central Jakarta. The giant spherical stage will be used for the concert titled YE Live in Jakarta on Saturday, October 24, 2026.

The news of the stage readiness was delivered by Marketing & Communications Lead of Raw Vision Collective, Karen Tjahja, at a press conference in the SCBD area, South Jakarta, Thursday (22/10/2026). According to her, the concert production preparations have been going very well and all performance needs have been prepared.

Globe Specs Same as Other Countries

Karen ensured that the size of the globe used in Jakarta was exactly the same as on Ye's stage in other countries, so the audience would not get a smaller experience. "And the size of the globe is exactly the same as in other countries," said Karen.

He also revealed the challenges of bringing the dome stage to Indonesia. Ye's team was said to be directly involved in production preparations with highly detailed specifications, while all the globe props were flown in specifically from abroad.

Regarding stage readiness, Karen said she had directly seen the condition of the globe inside the closed preparation area for recording. "With my own eyes last night, the globe was already ready," she said.

Besides the main stage, the promoter has set up additional LED screens so that the audience can watch Ye's performance from various angles of GBK Main Stadium.

Layered Security and Extended Transport

Ahead of the concert, Raw Vision Collective deployed more than 2,000 security personnel stationed from inside the ring road to inside the stadium. The promoter also coordinated with the DKI Jakarta Provincial Government and the National Police Headquarters to ensure the security and smooth running of the event.

Security is a top priority as several other events are taking place in the GBK area in close succession. The promoter has coordinated with organizers of other events to anticipate congestion.

To reduce congestion, spectators are urged to use public transportation. MRT Jakarta is extending operating hours until 01:30 WIB on the concert day, accompanied by increased trip frequency for the return flow. TransJakarta is adding trip frequency and bus capacity, while Bluebird Group is adding taxi fleets inside the event area.

Premiere and Only Concert in Southeast Asia

The October 24, 2026 concert will mark the debut performance of Ye — the stage name of Kanye West — in Indonesia. Jakarta is also the only Southeast Asian city included in Ye's official tour, making this concert a magnet for fans from various countries.

Official concert tickets are on sale starting at Rp1,875,000 via yejakarta.com and Loket.com.

item.title: KPK Searches Central Java BPK Office, Seizing Hundreds of Millions
item.description: KPK seized hundreds of millions of rupiah and documents in Central Java BPK searches tied to a Rp5 billion audit bribery case involving Klaten's regent.
item.content:encoded:
Hundreds of Millions Seized at Central Java BPK Office

The Corruption Eradication Commission (KPK) searched the Central Java Provincial Representative Office of the Supreme Audit Agency (BPK) in Semarang and two related private residences on Thursday (22/10/2026). The searches were an expansion of the investigation into suspected corruption within the Klaten Regency Government involving suspended Klaten Regent Hamenang Wajar Ismoyo.

KPK Spokesperson Budi Prasetyo stated that investigators discovered and confiscated hundreds of millions of rupiah in cash at the Central Java BPK office. In addition to cash, investigators secured documents and electronic evidence from the three searched locations.

Alleged Bribery to Remove Rp5 Billion Audit Findings

According to Budi, the evidence is suspected to be linked to bribery intended to wipe out BPK audit findings in Klaten Regency. A Central Java BPK audit in April 2026 uncovered honorarium overpayments totaling around Rp5 billion within the Klaten Regency Administration (Pemkab).

KPK previously revealed that Central Java BPK Representative Head Ahmad Luthfi H Rahmatullah allegedly demanded Rp600 million from Hamenang to remove those two findings from the audit report. Following negotiations, a sum of Rp400 million was agreed upon using the communication code 'AMIDIS'. In June 2026, BPK issued the audit report without the two findings.

Five Clusters, Three Suspects

The case originated from a KPK sting operation on 15 October 2026 that apprehended Hamenang, Ahmad Luthfi, and 21 other individuals. A day later, KPK named three suspects: Hamenang Wajar Ismoyo, Ahmad Luthfi H Rahmatullah, and private sector party Muhammad Amin Wahyu Utomo from PT Madani Winasis Creative.

KPK noted there are five clusters of alleged corruption: bribery to manipulate the BPK audit, goods and services procurement, Type C mineral mining permits, kickbacks from Regional Apparatus Organizations/Regional Work Units (OPD/SKPD), and levies related to tax collection fees. The investigation remains ongoing to trace fund flows and the relevance of the seized evidence.

item.title: M7.0 Tibet Earthquake Kills 16, Collapses 339 Homes
item.description: At least 16 people died and 32 were injured after a magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck northern Tibet, China, prompting a Level II emergency response Thursday.
item.content:encoded:
Latest Casualties and Damage

At least 16 people were killed and 32 others injured when a magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck northern Tibet on Thursday (10/22/2026) night local time, according to Chinese state media cited by CNN, NDTV, and Reuters. The official figures were released by the Nagqu city media office, citing municipal government officials.

A total of 339 homes reportedly collapsed due to the shaking, and rescue teams from police and fire departments continue setting up emergency tents to shelter displaced residents. The overall extent of the damage is still being assessed by local authorities.

Level II Emergency Response

The China Earthquake Administration activated a Level II emergency response — the country's second-highest tier. Railway authorities suspended train services passing through the affected area, according to a report by state broadcaster CCTV (China Central Television).

The main shock struck at 10:33 p.m. local time, with an epicenter roughly 183–191 kilometers east-northeast of Nagqu city, in a plateau region with an average elevation exceeding 4,800 meters. A magnitude 5.2 aftershock was recorded about 45 minutes later, according to data from the USGS (United States Geological Survey).

Strongest Earthquake Since January 2024

This earthquake is the strongest to hit China since an M7.1 quake struck a remote mountainous area of Xinjiang in January 2024, which killed three people and injured dozens of others. In December 2023, more than a hundred people died when an earthquake hit Jishishan County in Gansu Province — China's deadliest disaster in nearly a decade.

item.title: Antam Gold Price October 23, 2026 Holds at Rp2,550,000 per Gram
item.description: Antam Logam Mulia gold price held at Rp2,550,000 per gram on October 23, 2026, while global gold prices plunged to their lowest level since early August amid uncertainty over the Fed's rate decision.
item.content:encoded:
Antam gold price today

The price of gold bars produced by PT Aneka Tambang Tbk (Antam) Logam Mulia held steady in Friday's trading (23/10/2026). According to data from emasantam.id cited by industry.co.id, the price of 1-gram Antam gold stood at Rp2.550.000 per gram, unchanged from the previous day's trading.

The buyback price for Antam gold also remained unchanged at Rp2,365,000 per gram. Antam's reference price for pure silver held steady at Rp38,850 per gram.

Gold prices at Pegadaian

At Pegadaian, the prices of three gold products — Galeri 24, Antam, and UBS — were also unchanged this Friday. For the 1-gram size, Galeri 24 was sold at Rp2,499,000, Antam at Rp2,589,000, and UBS at Rp2,524,000, based on data updated Friday morning and cited by suaragarut.id.

The buyback price for 1 gram of Galeri 24 gold is recorded at Rp2,354,000, while Antam and UBS buyback prices stand at Rp2,328,000 per gram each. For the 0.5 gram size, Antam is sold at Rp1,345,000 and Galeri 24 at Rp1,311,000.

World gold plunges to lowest since August

Unlike the domestic market, world gold prices plunged in trading on October 22, 2026. Spot gold (XAU/USD) fell about 2.3-2.4 percent to the range of US$4,041-US$4,045 per troy ounce — the lowest level since early August 2026.

The weakening was triggered by rising oil prices and inflation concerns ahead of the US central bank's (The Fed) interest rate decision on October 27-28 and the release of PCE data on October 29. The strengthening of the US dollar and the rise in 10-year US Treasury yields to around 5.14 percent made gold — which offers no yield — less attractive to some investors.

Context of price trends

Antam gold prices briefly fell Rp4,000 per gram on October 22 — the third consecutive day of decline — before finally holding steady today. Meanwhile, on the Pluang platform, the buying price for 1 gram of Antam gold was recorded at Rp2,321,683 on the morning of October 23, down Rp4,374 from the previous day.

The divergence between international and domestic market movements shows that global price changes are not always immediately reflected in domestic precious metal products on the same day. The rupiah exchange rate, product pricing structures, and providers' pricing policies also influence domestic prices.

item.title: Rice Social Assistance Phase III Disbursed: 33.2 Million Recipients…
item.description: Perum Bulog, together with Commission IV of the House of Representatives (DPR) RI, launched Phase III Rice Food Assistance for the October–December 2026 allocation. A total of 33.2 million beneficiaries will receive 10 kg of rice per month; check the distribution schedule and how to check beneficiary status through official Kemensos channels.
item.content:encoded:
Third Phase of Rice Food Assistance Officially Launched

Perum Bulog together with Commission IV of the DPR RI officially launched the distribution of Stage III Rice Food Assistance for the October, November, and December 2026 allocation. The launch was held at the Potorono Village Hall, Banguntapan District, Bantul Regency, Special Region of Yogyakarta, on Tuesday (20/10/2026), with the approval of President Prabowo Subianto. Approximately 33.2 million Food Assistance Beneficiaries (PBP) across Indonesia are the targets of this program.

Each recipient receives 10 kilograms of rice per month, or a total of 30 kilograms over three months of distribution. The program is one of the instruments for protecting people's purchasing power amid household needs that continue to depend on the stability of staple food prices.

33.2 Million Recipients, Each to Receive 30 Kg of Rice

The launch in Bantul was attended by House Commission IV Chairwoman Siti Hediati Soeharto (Titiek Soeharto) and Perum Bulog President Director Ahmad Rizal Ramdhani. "The continuation of food assistance through the end of the year is a form of President Prabowo Subianto's attention to public welfare," Titiek said.

Rizal emphasized that Bulog is ready to carry out the government's assignment by optimizing stocks, its warehousing network, and distribution across Indonesia. "Food assistance will resume for the October, November, and December 2026 allocations," he said.

Specifically for the Special Region of Yogyakarta, the aid allocation reaches 522,956 PBP or 15,688,680 kilograms of rice. Bantul Regency covers 138,702 PBP with a total of 4,161,060 kilograms, while Potorono Village accounts for 716 PBP with 21,480 kilograms. Distribution in DIY reaches four regencies, namely Bantul, Sleman, Kulon Progo, and Gunungkidul.

How to Check Food Assistance Recipient Status

The surge in searches for "cek bansos ktp" on Google Trends Indonesia shows that many citizens want to verify their membership status. The Ministry of Social Affairs provides the official page cekbansos.kemensos.go.id: fill in the domicile area from province down to village or kelurahan, enter the beneficiary's name as per KTP, type the 16-digit NIK, then fill in the captcha code.

Besides the website, checks can be carried out through the Cek Bansos application downloaded from the Google Play Store or Apple App Store by registering with a NIK and family card number. The public is urged to use only official channels and to be wary of fake links that request personal data or verification codes.

Distribution Backed by Government Rice Reserves

The third phase of distribution is supported by the Government Rice Reserve (CBP) managed by Bulog. Bulog is strengthening coordination with the central government, regional governments, and relevant parties to ensure that assistance is delivered to eligible recipients in the correct quantity and quality in accordance with regulations.

Rizal emphasized the distribution principles upheld by Bulog: aid must reach people in need with good quality, in the right quantity, and at the right time. With a target of 33.2 million beneficiaries spread across various regions, accurate beneficiary data and quality oversight are key to the program's success through December 2026.

item.title: Bournemouth Thrash AC Milan 3-0 in Europa League
item.description: Bournemouth beat AC Milan 3-0 on Europa League matchday 3 at Vitality Stadium, Friday (23/10/2026) early morning WIB. Penalties from Justin Kluivert (8') and Marcus Tavernier (32') plus Amine Adli's goal (84') sealed the win; Milan goalkeeper Mike Maignan was sent off in the 27th minute.
item.content:encoded:
Kluivert and Tavernier Strike from the Spot

Bournemouth were dominant from the opening minutes. Hosting AC Milan on matchday 3 of the 2026/2027 UEFA Europa League league phase at Vitality Stadium, Friday (23/10/2026) early morning WIB, the hosts took the lead in the 8th minute: Evanilson was fouled in the box in the 6th minute, VAR confirmed the decision, and Justin Kluivert calmly converted the penalty.

Disaster struck Milan in the 27th minute. Goalkeeper Mike Maignan shoved Tyler Adams in the face with both hands as Bournemouth prepared to take a corner. Referee Vassilis Fotias immediately produced a red card and awarded a second penalty to the hosts; the decision was confirmed by VAR. Backup goalkeeper Lorenzo Torriani came on in the 32nd minute for Omari Hutchinson, but Marcus Tavernier beat him from the spot anyway. The first half ended 2-0.

Maignan Sent Off for Shoving Adams

The red-card incident was the game's turning point. Adams stood directly in front of Maignan at the corner, and the goalkeeper's reaction was excessive: a two-handed shove to the face of the US international left him on the ground. Fotias had no hesitation in showing a straight red, while Adams himself was booked in the 29th minute for his role in the incident.

The match also pitted two USMNT teammates against each other: Adams started in Bournemouth's midfield, while Yunus Musah started for Milan. Christian Pulisic, the Americans' other star, began the game on the Rossoneri bench. Down to 10 men from the 27th minute, Milan were virtually unable to escape the hosts' pressure.

Adli Seals Emphatic 3-0 Win

Bournemouth did not ease off in the second half. Amine Adli, introduced in the 77th minute for Alex Tóth, scored the third goal in the 84th minute to seal the emphatic 3-0 victory. The scoreline stood until the final whistle.

The hosts' dominance was reflected clearly in the numbers: 64%-36% possession, 20 shots to 3, seven on target to none for Milan, and expected goals of 3.18 to 0.17. AC Milan left England without a single shot on target and with a costly red card — a night to forget for Ruben Amorim's side.

item.title: BBC: RSF Deliberately Destroyed 43 Hospitals in El-Fasher
item.description: A BBC probe reveals RSF paramilitaries systematically destroyed el-Fasher's health system in Darfur, killing 55 medics in 43 attacks. The UN cites war crimes.
item.content:encoded:
43 Attacks on Healthcare Facilities

A BBC investigation published on October 23, 2026, found evidence that fighters from the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) paramilitary systematically destroyed the healthcare system in el-Fasher, a city in Darfur, western Sudan, during a prolonged siege and takeover a year ago. The BBC documented at least 43 separate attacks on hospitals and healthcare facilities from May 2024 to October 2025—with several sites targeted repeatedly.

The strikes were carried out using artillery shelling and drones, including precision drones. The Saudi Hospital—the last remaining operational facility—was bombed repeatedly up to 25 times over several days, leaving medical personnel to perform Caesarean sections under only the light of mobile phones. South Hospital was raided by the RSF on June 8, 2024: staff members were beaten, and its director general, Izzeldin Ahmed Dawaud Asow, was assaulted until he played dead to survive.

55 Medics Killed, UN Warns of War Crimes

Between April 2023 and October 2025, 120 healthcare workers were wounded, 55 killed, and 10 forcibly disappeared or abducted. More than 460 patients and accompanying persons are believed to have died during hospital raids on October 25, 2025, when the RSF captured the city.

UN (United Nations) Human Rights Chief Volker Türk called the BBC findings 'deeply disturbing' and stated that repeated attacks on civilian infrastructure, including medical facilities, constitute grave breaches of international humanitarian law that 'may amount to war crimes.' Sudan's civil war erupted in April 2023 between the RSF and the Sudanese military.

RSF Rejects Findings, Calls Them Propaganda

The RSF rejected the BBC findings. The paramilitary group's health minister, Dr. Alaa Eldin Nugud, described the allegations as propaganda and a 'continuation of lies' by the national army and its allies aimed at tarnishing the RSF's reputation.

He also claimed South Hospital was used as a military base—an assertion that the BBC noted was unsupported by independent evidence. The BBC interviewed six doctors who were in el-Fasher during the siege for this investigation.

item.title: CATL Battery Factory in Karawang Ready to Be Inaugurated by Prabowo
item.description: The electric vehicle battery ecosystem plant of PT CATIB in Karawang, a collaboration between battery giant CATL and Indonesian state-owned enterprises, has been completed and is awaiting the inauguration schedule of President Prabowo Subianto. With an initial capacity of 6.9 GWh and an investment of US$6 billion, the plant marks Indonesia's leap from a raw nickel exporter to a player in the global battery supply chain.
item.content:encoded:
Waiting for the President's Schedule

Minister of Energy and Mineral Resources Bahlil Lahadalia confirmed that the electric vehicle battery ecosystem factory in Karawang has been fully completed and is ready to be inaugurated. "It is ready to be inaugurated. We are just waiting for the right time from the President. The factory is finished," Bahlil said at the Presidential Palace Complex, Jakarta, Monday (19/10/2026).

The facility was built through a partnership between China's CATL and an Indonesian state-owned enterprise, with the groundbreaking ceremony led by President Prabowo Subianto about a year earlier. Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources Secretary-General Ahmad Erani Yustika confirmed that the battery cell plant developed by PT CATIB has been operational — the commissioning and gradual operation phase has been underway since August 2026.

US$6 Billion Dragon Project

PT CATIB was established as a joint venture between Indonesia Battery Corporation (IBC) and Ningbo Contemporary Brunp Lygend Co. Ltd. (CBL) — a consortium of Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. Limited (CATL), Brunp, and Lygend. The investment value of the project, dubbed the Dragon Project, is estimated at US$6 billion, or approximately Rp98.58 trillion.

The production facility stands in the Artha Industrial Hills (AIH) area, Karawang Regency, on a 43-hectare plot of land, encompassing a module & pack plant as well as a cell plant. "CATIB's capacity in this first phase is 6.9 GWh and we will soon expand it to at least 15 GWh," said Aditya Farhan Arif, President Director of IBC. The conversion of 15 GWh is equivalent to batteries for approximately 250 thousand electric vehicles.

The product lineup includes battery cells, modules, packs, and Battery Energy Storage System (BESS). The President Director of IBC also ensured that the market is ready to absorb it: buyers are already in place and trial production is underway at the factory.

Peak of Nickel Downstreaming

The inauguration of the Karawang plant will make it the second battery ecosystem factory in Indonesia. The first facility involved LG and was built when Bahlil was still serving as Minister of Investment. CATIB's presence marks a gradual shift in Indonesia's nickel value chain: from ore smelting and intermediate products such as ferronickel and nickel matte, toward battery cell assembly, which carries far greater added value.

This momentum aligns with the bright outlook for downstream trade. Bloomberg Technoz (21/10/2026) reports that Indonesia's nickel and lithium battery component exports in 2026 are projected to surpass Rp899 trillion, while InvestorTrust (19/10/2026) notes that global nickel demand is projected to rise 21.39 percent.

For international readers, the message is clear: Indonesia is no longer merely exporting raw materials. With two battery ecosystem plants and an integrated supply chain from mine to cell, Indonesia is positioning itself as one of the world's electric vehicle battery manufacturing hubs.

item.title: Prabowo Threatens to Revoke Concessions of Repeat Fire Violators
item.description: President Prabowo Subianto slammed foreign critics over forest fires linked to their firms and vowed to revoke concessions of those violating rules up to 19 times.
item.content:encoded:
Rebuke for Foreign Nations

President Prabowo Subianto reprimanded several nations that mock and insult Indonesia over forest and land fires (karhutla). In fact, he stated, companies originating from those very countries share responsibility for the fires sweeping through multiple regions in Indonesia.

'Several countries mock us, insult us, and so forth. Yet many of their own companies are responsible here,' Prabowo said while attending the 2026 National Coordination Meeting of the Regional Financial Access Acceleration Team (TPAKD - Tim Percepatan Akses Keuangan Daerah) at JIExpo Kemayoran, Jakarta, on Thursday (22/10/2026).

Threat to Revoke Concessions of 19-Time Violators

On the same occasion, Prabowo revealed that there are concession-holding companies that have repeatedly violated regulations up to 19 times. He emphasized that he would not hesitate to revoke the business permits of companies proven to have committed violations causing forest and land fires. 'Whoever violates the rules, that's it, just revoke it. I won't hesitate, I will simply revoke them later,' he asserted.

Prabowo also opened up the possibility of transferring the management of revoked lands or plantations to Indonesian human resources. According to him, young Indonesians are capable of managing these plantations, and it would be far better managed independently out of love for the homeland.

Staying Focused on Fire Mitigation

Despite delivering harsh criticism, Prabowo stressed that the government remains focused on handling forest and land fires by mobilizing the Indonesian National Armed Forces (TNI - Tentara Nasional Indonesia), the Indonesian National Police (Polri - Kepolisian Negara Republik Indonesia), and local governments, emphasizing that the government takes responsibility for the mitigation efforts.

He also reminded that the impact of the fires is not only environmental damage, but also threatens public health, especially children in affected areas. Prabowo expressed his belief that local communities relying on forests and lands in Kalimantan would not damage their own living environments, as they are the ones who suffer the most.

Forest and land fires have affected several regions across Sumatra, Kalimantan, Java, and Papua over the past four months. Although suppression efforts continue, hotspots in several areas are reportedly not yet fully extinguished, and haze still blankets residential areas, beginning to impair public health.

item.title: Lt. Col. Arman Named Suspect in Military Housing Gambling Base Case
item.description: Pomdam Jaya detained Lt. Col. Arman for allegedly leasing military housing in East Jakarta to civilians for an online gambling den. Eleven were arrested.
item.content:encoded:
Lt. Col. Arman Named Suspect and Detained

The Military Police of the Jayakarta Regional Military Command (Pomdam Jaya/Jayakarta) has named Lieutenant Colonel of Infantry (Letkol Inf) Arman a suspect in a case involving the unauthorized leasing of military official housing used as an online gambling headquarters. The suspect designation was announced by the Commander of Pomdam Jaya/Jayakarta (Danpomdam Jaya/Jayakarta), Colonel of Military Police (Kolonel Cpm) Unggul Wahyudi, to journalists at Jakarta Regional Police Headquarters (Polda Metro Jaya) on Wednesday (21/10/2026).

"Yes, he has officially been named a suspect. It is currently being processed. We have detained him at Pomdam. Yes, there are elements of violation regarding the leasing of official housing," Unggul said. Lt. Col. Arman, who serves as the Section Head of Intelligence for Permanent Garrison (Kasi Intel Gartap) 1/Jakarta, is currently being held at Pomdam Jaya for questioning.

Cijantung Official Quarters Turned into Online Gambling Base

The official residence in question is located in the Army Housing Complex (KPAD - Kompleks Perumahan Angkatan Darat) in Cijantung, East Jakarta. The house, owned by the Indonesian Army (TNI AD - Tentara Nasional Indonesia Angkatan Darat), was leased to civilians and allegedly converted into an operational center for online gambling, equipped with computer equipment across several rooms.

"The tenants were ordinary people (civilians), the general public," Unggul said. The case unfolded after the Indonesian Army received reports of suspicious activities within the military residential compound. In early October 2026, personnel from the East Jakarta Military District Command (Kodim 0505/Jakarta Timur) alongside regional units raided the location and seized several items of evidence.

During the bust, 11 civilians consisting of six men and five women were apprehended and taken to the Military Police Detachment (Denpom - Detasemen Polisi Militer) for examination. Officers confiscated 32 computer units, 14 mobile phones, and nine national identity cards (KTP - Kartu Tanda Penduduk) allegedly used to operate the online gambling network.

Indonesian Military Investigates Rogue Personnel Involvement

The Indonesian National Armed Forces (TNI - Tentara Nasional Indonesia) is continuing to investigate when the official residence was first leased and repurposed as an online gambling base, including potential involvement of other parties. Head of Information for Kodam Jaya (Kapendam Jaya) Lieutenant Colonel of Artillery (Letkol Arh) Noor Ishak noted that the duration and timeline of the lease remain central to Pomdam Jaya's ongoing inquiry.

Head of the Indonesian Military Information Center (Kapuspen TNI) Brigadier General Muhammad Nas stressed that service members implicated in online gambling will face penalties. "The legal process is underway; sanctions will definitely be handed down commensurate with the gravity of the legal violation," Nas stated. The TNI emphasized that it will not tolerate the misuse of state assets by rogue soldiers.

The case has drawn widespread public scrutiny as it implicates an active mid-ranking officer from the garrison intelligence corps and exploited state assets situated in the heart of a military residential enclave. The Army stated that supervision over official housing assets will be tightened to prevent similar incidents from recurring, pending the outcome of Pomdam Jaya's ongoing investigation.

item.title: Isco Fires Real Betis Past Feyenoord 1-0, Perfect 9 Points
item.description: Real Betis beat Feyenoord 1-0 on Champions League matchday 3 at the Estadio de La Cartuja, early Thursday (22/10/2026) WIB. Isco's 58th-minute penalty sealed a perfect 9-point start; the captain became the first Betis player to score in consecutive UCL matches.
item.content:encoded:
Isco's Penalty Makes the Difference

Real Betis continued their perfect start to the 2026/2027 Champions League. At the Estadio de La Cartuja, early Thursday (22/10/2026) WIB, Los Verdiblancos edged Feyenoord 1-0 on league-phase matchday 3.

Betis dominated the first half. Abde Ezzalzouli and Troy Parrott took turns threatening, but goalkeeper Tjark Ernst was heroic — including a superb stop to deny Marc Bartra's stinging strike from distance. Feyenoord actually had a golden chance through Gjivai Zechiel, but he blazed over from six yards.

The deadlock was broken in the 58th minute. The referee pointed to the spot after Abde forced Jeremiah St. Juste into a handball inside the area. Isco stepped up and made no mistake, sending Ernst the wrong way. The goal made the captain the first Real Betis player to score in consecutive Champions League matches.

Valles Stands Tall, Feyenoord Frustrated

Trailing, Giovanni van Bronckhorst's Feyenoord raised the intensity and pressed higher. Anis Hadj Moussa was a constant threat on the flank, but goalkeeper Alvaro Valles stood tall — he denied Bartra from close range late on and kept his clean sheet intact until the final whistle.

The win gave Real Betis a perfect nine points from three league-phase matches, with only one defeat in their last nine games in all competitions. Feyenoord, meanwhile, dropped outside the top 24 and lost both of their Spanish away ties this season.

item.title: Sahroni: Intent Must Define Corruption, Not Just State Losses
item.description: House Commission III Deputy Chair Ahmad Sahroni backed separating state losses from corruption, urging intent-based criteria and a Tipikor Law revision.
item.content:encoded:
Sahroni: Separate state business from official wrongdoing

Deputy Chair of Commission III of the House of Representatives of the Republic of Indonesia (DPR RI) Ahmad Sahroni expressed his support for the proposal by National Economic Council (DEN) Chair Luhut Binsar Pandjaitan to separate the definition of state financial losses from the crime of corruption. Sahroni made the statement in remarks to the media on Thursday (22/10/2026), as quoted by detikNews.

"I agree with what Pak Luhut said; the benchmark for corruption offenses must distinguish between state business and criminal offenses committed by state officials," Sahroni said. According to the NasDem Party politician, it is time for Indonesia's corruption case standards to differentiate between normal business risks faced by state-owned enterprises and pure criminal acts committed by public officials for personal gain.

Benchmark: malicious intent, not merely state losses

Sahroni argued that establishing corruption must remain anchored in malicious intent (mens rea) and direct harm to the broader public. He cited the example of regional leaders who ought to prioritize the public interest but instead take assets for personal benefit. "We need to examine the measure of malicious intent," he noted.

He also urged that Luhut's idea be scrutinized thoroughly by legal experts and policymakers to build a solid foundation. "Pak Luhut's recommendation must be examined in depth to establish a clear distinction between actions taken in the state's interest and corruption that clearly harms the public. This must be followed up with a revision of the Corruption Eradication Law (UU Tipikor) to provide a strong legal basis for law enforcement officials (APH)," he explained.

Luhut's proposal and Presidential approval

Earlier, Luhut submitted a proposal to study revising the definition of corruption to President Prabowo Subianto. In statements delivered at the Merdeka Palace Complex in Jakarta, Luhut said the President had approved the study prepared by the National Economic Council team. Luhut proposed that state losses should not automatically be categorized as corruption offenses.

The foundation for the proposal refers to the United Nations Convention Against Corruption (UNCAC), which Indonesia ratified through Law No. 7 of 2006. According to Luhut, the convention specifically defines corruption as bribery, not state financial loss. He noted that Indonesia remains one of the few countries that incorporates state financial loss as an element of corruption, thereby encumbering institutions such as Danantara when executing business decisions.

Debate: legal certainty versus public accountability

Sahroni's statements have reignited debate over the boundary between state financial losses, commercial business risks, and conduct meeting the elements of criminal corruption. On one hand, legal certainty is necessary to ensure policymakers are not afraid to take professional decisions.

On the other hand, regulatory changes must still guarantee accountability in managing state finances without opening loopholes for corrupt actors to evade responsibility. Therefore, comprehensive scrutiny by legal scholars is considered essential before any revision of the Corruption Eradication Law is officially launched.

item.title: Club Brugge Thrash Lens 3-0, Yet Leko Furious at Half-Time
item.description: Club Brugge beat RC Lens 3-0 on Champions League matchday 3 at the Jan Breydelstadion, early Thursday (22/10/2026) WIB. Goals from Hans Vanaken (45+3'), Joaquin Seys (50') and Carlos Forbs (72') took Brugge to 6 points; coach Ivan Leko remained furious at half-time, and the match was marred by a flare incident involving Lens fans.
item.content:encoded:
Vanaken's Stoppage-Time Breakthrough

Club Brugge continued their fine run in the 2026/2027 Champions League. At the Jan Breydelstadion, early Thursday (22/10/2026) WIB, Ivan Leko's side thrashed RC Lens 3-0 on league-phase matchday 3.

The first half was tight. Lens stayed disciplined and threatened through Junior Kadile, but Yann Sommer stood firm in goal. The deadlock was broken in stoppage time: in the 45th+3rd minute, captain Hans Vanaken pounced on a loose ball inside the penalty area and fired a low shot beyond goalkeeper Risser.

Second-Half Blitz: Seys and Forbs

Brugge emerged with different energy after the restart. Five minutes into the second half, Joaquin Seys doubled the lead — his first effort was saved by Risser, but he converted the rebound to make it 2-0.

Lens tried to respond by introducing Jean-Clair Todibo and Florian Thauvin, but Brugge's midfield controlled the tempo comfortably. In the 72nd minute, Carlos Forbs sealed the victory with a composed finish after being released by substitute Hugo Vetlesen. The third goal capped a perfect evening for the hosts.

Leko's Fury and Crowd Trouble

The convincing win took Club Brugge to six points from three matches, following last week's dramatic 4-3 victory at Inter Milan. Yet coach Ivan Leko was far from satisfied: defender Brandon Mechele revealed the coach was furious in the dressing room at half-time despite the lead. 'Leko woke us up at half-time. It was pretty intense,' Mechele told Belgian reporters.

The match was also marred by trouble in the stands. Lens supporters lit flares and threw them towards the section reserved for supporters with disabilities, injuring a steward and briefly halting play in the first half. Bruges police said they would examine camera footage to identify those responsible.

item.title: Galatasaray Comeback to Beat Lille 4-2, Osimhen Nets vs Former Club
item.description: Galatasaray beat Lille 4-2 on Champions League matchday 3 at Stade Pierre-Mauroy early on Thursday (22/10/2026) WIB. Goals from Yunus Akgün (2'), Aleksey Batrakov (44'), a Berke Özer own goal (52') and Victor Osimhen (61') overturned the hosts' 2-1 lead earned through Soriba Diaoune's brace (7', 39'). Galatasaray's first win of the season ended a run of five straight away defeats.
item.content:encoded:
Six Goals in a Pulsating Thriller

Galatasaray claimed their first Champions League win of the season in dramatic fashion. Visiting Stade Pierre-Mauroy early on Thursday (22/10/2026) WIB, Okan Buruk's side beat Lille 4-2 on Champions League 2026/2027 league-phase matchday 3 in a six-goal thriller.

The game was just two minutes old when Yunus Akgün put Galatasaray ahead. Lille responded quickly through Soriba Diaoune, who levelled in the 7th minute from Alexsandro's pass. The Lille striker struck again in the 39th minute to turn the game around and give the hosts a 2-1 lead.

But Lille's lead vanished before half-time. Aleksey Batrakov headed home Roland Sallai's cross in the 44th minute to make it 2-2. Seven minutes after the restart, disaster struck the hosts: goalkeeper Berke Özer failed to deal with a corner situation and the ball went into his own net. Victor Osimhen sealed the 4-2 win with a powerful strike in the 61st minute from Barış Alper Yılmaz's assist.

Osimhen Haunts His Former Club

Osimhen's goal carried extra meaning as Lille are his former club. The Nigeria striker muted his celebration out of respect for the home crowd. Earlier, Osimhen had nearly scored sooner, but his penalty award in the 27th minute was overturned after the referee's VAR review found no foul.

Although Lille dominated with 56% possession and 15 shots, Galatasaray's ruthless efficiency proved decisive. All four of the visitors' shots on target ended up in the net — a deadly display of finishing.

Soriba Diaoune was the hosts' best player with his brace, each goal the product of fine link-up play with Alexsandro and Hákon Arnar Haraldsson. Unfortunately, the striker's double was not enough to save Lille from defeat.

First Win for Gala, Lille Sink Deeper

The victory ended Galatasaray's run of five consecutive away defeats in the Champions League and earned them their first three points of the season. Lille, in contrast, suffered a third straight home defeat in UEFA competition and remain pointless — a disappointing start for Bruno Génésio's side.

Galatasaray can now push up the league-phase standings, while Lille must regroup quickly to keep their qualification hopes alive. Both teams still have five matches left to decide their fate in Europe's elite competition this season.

item.title: '98 Volunteer Group Backs Prabowo, Stays Ready to Criticize
item.description: Marking two years of the Prabowo-Gibran administration, the 98 Resolution Network pledged conditional support and vowed open critique if policies harm citizens.
item.content:encoded:
'Real Action' statement on two years of administration

A network calling itself the 98 Resolution Network released a statement entitled 'Real Action of 2 Years of the Prabowo-Gibran Administration: One Resolve to Grow with the People, Prosper Together' on Wednesday (21/10/2026). The volunteer group supporting President Prabowo Subianto and Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka outlined several policies deemed significant milestones during the administration's two-year tenure.

The statement was initiated by Haris Rusly Moti alongside Wahab Talaohu, Eli Salomo Sinaga, and dozens of other activists. Highlighted areas included strengthening the people's economy, managing natural resources, education, health, and providing housing.

Article 33 as the grundnorm of economic democracy

The 98 Resolution Network assessed that the Prabowo-Gibran administration is striving to strengthen economic democracy by placing the public as the primary drivers of development. They linked this policy direction to Article 33 of the UUD 1945 (1945 Constitution), which governs state control over vital sectors of production and natural resources for the greatest prosperity of the people.

According to them, 'if political democratization, freedom, and equality in the political arena do not proceed simultaneously with the economic democratization agenda, what actually emerges is the practice of pseudo-democracy.' The network also warned that a development model reliant on raw material exports and imported consumption goods carries risks. 'Such a model risks positioning Indonesia as a coolie nation among nations,' they wrote.

The statement outlined nine monitoring agendas, ranging from institutionalizing economic democracy and restoring the public as subjects of development, to industrial downstreaming and domestic capital consolidation via BPI Danantara (Daya Anagata Nusantara Investment Management Agency) and DHE (Export Proceeds Foreign Exchange) regulations. Highlighted initiatives included the MBG (Free Nutritious Meal) program, Red and White Village Cooperatives, Red and White Fishing Villages, and subsidized housing.

Conditional support in the style of a critical partner

While declaring support, the 98 Resolution Network emphasized that their backing remains limited and conditional. If government policies are judged contrary to the constitution or detrimental to the broader public interest, they affirmed their intention to voice critical views openly.

The network also asserted they will not assume positions in the cabinet or state institutions, ensuring their oversight role remains independent and sharp. They position themselves as critical partners and part of the public oversight ecosystem, noting guaranteed freedom of expression as a prerequisite for a healthy democracy.

item.title: KPK Detains 7 North Sumatra BBPJN Officials in Road Project Bribery…
item.description: The KPK detained seven of eight new suspects in the alleged bribery case involving road projects under the North Sumatra BBPJN for the 2023-2025 period on Thursday (22/10/2026). The seven suspects were detained for an initial 20 days until 10 November 2026; one suspect failed to appear and has been summoned again for 26 October.
item.content:encoded:
Seven Suspects Detained for 20 Days

The Corruption Eradication Commission (KPK) has detained seven new suspects in the expanded investigation into the alleged bribery and gratification case involving road projects at the National Road Implementation Center (BBPJN) of North Sumatra for the 2023-2025 period.

The announcement of the detention was delivered by Acting KPK Director of Investigation Achmad Taufik Husein during a press conference at the KPK Red and White Building, Jakarta, Thursday (22/10/2026). "Today seven suspects who were present were subsequently subjected to coercive measures in the form of detention by investigators," said Achmad Taufik.

The seven suspects were detained for an initial 20-day period, from October 22 to November 10, 2026, at the KPK's Red and White Building Detention Center for investigation purposes.

Eight New Suspects Since September 30

The KPK named eight new suspects in this case on September 30, 2026. "On September 30, 2026, the KPK again named eight people as suspects," said Achmad Taufik. The designation was made after investigators found sufficient evidence from the facts presented at trial in the previous case as well as new evidence during the investigation process.

Seven suspects who attended and were immediately detained are Stanley Cicero Haggard Tuapattinaja, Head of BBPJN North Sumatra for the period September 2024 to 28 June 2025; Rahmad Parulian, Head of Work Unit Region I of BBPJN North Sumatra; Faisal, Commitment-Making Official (PPK) 1.1 of BBPJN North Sumatra Region I; and Heri Handoko, PPK 1.2 of BBPJN North Sumatra Region I.

The other three are T. Rahmansyah Putra, Head of the National Road Implementation Work Unit for Region II of North Sumatra; Manaek Manalu, PPK 2.2 of BBPJN North Sumatra Region II; and Munson Ponter Paulus, PPK 1.4 of the Work Unit for Region I of BBPJN North Sumatra.

Meanwhile, the eighth suspect, Dicky Erlangga, who serves as Head of the PJN Work Unit for Region I of the North Sumatra BBPJN, did not comply with the investigators' summons. The KPK will issue a second summons for his questioning on Monday, October 26, 2026, in accordance with the provisions of criminal procedure law.

Development of the June 2025 OTT

This case is an expansion of the KPK's sting operation (OTT) on June 26, 2025, concerning alleged corruption in six road projects in North Sumatra worth approximately Rp231.8 billion.

In the development of the investigation, the KPK is probing allegations of conditioning road construction projects and receiving money related to the case. Media reported an alleged total fee of Rp8.3 billion in the development of this case.

The two suspects are charged with violating provisions of the Corruption Eradication Law. The KPK stated that the investigation is still ongoing to trace the accountability of parties involved in the alleged irregularities in the infrastructure procurement.

item.title: US Pulls Embassy Staff from Saudi Arabia as Houthi Attacks Intensify
item.description: The United States Department of State on Wednesday (10/21/2026) ordered non-essential personnel and their family members to leave Saudi Arabia. The move came amid intensifying Houthi attacks on Saudi civilian airports and critical infrastructure, including a drone attack on Wednesday that killed two foreign workers at the Shaybah oil field.
item.content:encoded:
State Department issues formal withdrawal order

The United States Department of State on Wednesday (10/21/2026) ordered non-essential personnel and their family members to leave Saudi Arabia. Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott confirmed the order in a post on X.

According to Pigott, the order applies to 'non-emergency US government employees and their family members in Saudi Arabia only.' He linked the move to attacks by Iran-backed Houthis against Saudi Arabia, including strikes on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure that caused casualties and severe travel disruptions.

'The safety and security of Department personnel and their families remain our highest priority,' Pigott said, as quoted by AFP.

Houthi attacks intensify, two foreign workers killed

On the same day, Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry said debris from the successful interception of a drone targeting an oil facility killed two people — a Filipino and a Nepali — and injured two others. The ministry did not say who launched the drone aimed at the Shaybah oil field near the United Arab Emirates border.

According to AFP, Saudi Arabia has faced near-daily attacks this month from Iran-backed Houthis. Among them was a strike on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport described as the deadliest attack on the Kingdom in years — the October 13-14 attack that killed 13 people and injured hundreds.

The US Embassy in Riyadh also issued a security alert on Wednesday about possible further Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia. According to CNN, US government employees working in Saudi Arabia now require special authorization from the Chief of Mission to use any airport in the Kingdom following recent missile and drone attacks.

Families of staff in other Gulf states also ordered to leave

A diplomatic source told AFP that 'all American staff and their families have been ordered to depart from the US embassy' in Saudi Arabia, and that families of embassy staff were also ordered to leave the United Arab Emirates, Jordan, Qatar, and Bahrain — countries the source said were targeted by Iran in the Middle East war.

Four US officials speaking to Reuters said US missions in other Gulf states would also order family members to leave. Pigott himself did not address changes at missions outside Saudi Arabia.

Reuters noted Washington had returned some diplomatic personnel to the region in recent months, after many were pulled out when Iran launched attacks on US facilities following the US-Israeli war on Iran that began in late February. AFP said the US previously ordered non-essential staff to leave the Gulf region ahead of the start of its war against Iran and again in July, before President Donald Trump called off a new wave of strikes.

An escalation Indonesians in the Gulf should watch

The withdrawal order marks a serious escalation signal in a conflict rooted in the collapse of Yemen's four-year truce in June. The war triggered by US-Israeli attacks on Iran has snarled global energy trade and shaken Gulf economies.

For Indonesia, Saudi Arabia is a top destination for migrant workers and umrah pilgrims — so the escalation of attacks on airports and public facilities in the Kingdom adds to the list of concerns for Indonesians across the Gulf region.
